page: Microsoft Azure DC96as_v6 is an x86_64 general-purpose virtual machine powered by AMD processors running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance is provisioned with 96 dedicated vCPUs and 384.0 GB of system memory, maintaining a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory allocation of 4.0 GB RAM per core. Hardware acceleration is absent, with zero GPUs included in the configuration.

This server type does not feature integrated local storage, requiring attached remote disks for file operations. The platform supports Premium Storage to enable high-throughput persistent storage interfaces. Network integration does not supply complimentary public IPv4 addresses, necessitating external configuration for inbound internet-facing connectivity.

Cost efficiency is driven by the high density of dedicated cores combined with a balanced memory allocation, allowing resource consolidation without investing in unused local storage or accelerator hardware. The architectural profile is suited for highly threaded enterprise workloads, heavy backend web serving, enterprise application servers, and continuous integration pipelines operating with remote persistent storage volumes.
description: Microsoft Azure DC96as_v6 is a general-purpose virtual machine powered by AMD x86_64 processors on the Microsoft Hyper-V platform. It offers 96 dedicated vCPUs paired with 384.0 GB of system memory, matching a balanced general-purpose allocation of 4.0 GB per vCPU. The instance contains no integrated GPUs and has no local ephemeral storage, utilizing Azure Premium Storage compatibility for persistent drive operations. Networking provisions omit complimentary public IPv4 addresses, requiring dedicated routing for external network traffic. By providing high dedicated core density without the overhead of physical local disks or specialized accelerators, the instance offers cost-efficient compute capacity for scaled deployments. Microsoft Azure DC96as_v6 is designed for heavy multi-threaded enterprise workloads, large-scale application tiers, container orchestration nodes, and distributed computing tasks relying on networked storage architectures.
